entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Hon'Ble Sri Justice C.V.Bhaskar Reddy
 Writ Petition No.22435 of 2023
Order:

The present writ petition has been filed seeking the following relief:-
"...to issue a writ or order/s more particularly one in the nature of Writ of Mandamus declaring action of respondent No 5 in issuing the Look Out Circular No.183/LOC/CCS-DD/HYD/2019 dated 30-08-2019 at the request of respondent No.3 and imposing a travel ban on the petitioner and further continuing the Lookout circular beyond the period of one year as illegal, arbitrary, unconstitutional,
highhanded without authority without jurisdiction and in violation of principles of natural justice apart from being violative of Articles 14, 19 and 21 of the Constitution of India, in violation of the provisions of passport act 1967 and consequently to set aside the Look Out Circular No. 183/LOC/ CCS-DD/HYD/2019 dated 30-08-2019 issued by the respondent No.5 against the petitioner..."

2. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner has been arrayed as Accused No.1 in Crime No.494 of 2019 on the file of Banjara Hills Police Station, which was registered on the basis of a complaint lodged by Aravind Kumar Shaw, for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 465,
467 and 471 of IPC.

He further submits that during the course of investigation, police arrested the petitioner and sent him to judicial custody and thereafter, the petitioner filed bail application vide Crl.M.P.No.3329 of 2019 on the file of III Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, at Hyderabad and the said Crl.M.P was allowed vide order dated 19.10.2019 and the petitioner/A.1 was ordered to be released on bail on his executing bond for Rs.1,00,000/- with two cash sureties each in the form of FDR obtained from any nationalized bank.

entities.text: III Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, at Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Further, the petitioner was directed to appear before the Station House Officer, Banjara Hills Police Station once in a week on every Sunday at 10.00 AM for a period of one month or till filing of the charge sheet, whichever is earlier.
It is submitted that petitioner needs to travel to Dubai and other countries on business meetings.
However, the respondent No.5 has issued lookout circular No.183/LOC/CCS-DD/HYD/2019 dated 30-08-2019 at the request of respondent No.3 and imposed a travel ban on the petitioner.
It is further submitted that the petitioner is regularly appearing before the concerned officer as per the directions of this Court.

Despite the same, the LOC issued against the petitioner is still continuing, due to which he is not in a position to travel to foreign country, thereby affecting his livelihood and therefore, this action of the respondents police is highly arbitrary in a way interfering with the life and liberty of the petitioner.
3. Heard both sides and perused the record.

sentences.text: Basing on the orders passed by a learned Single Judge of this Court, the Director General of Police has issued instructions to all the concerned by Circular Memorandum dated 01.07.2022 vide C.No.3089/C-3/IP/CID/2019-22, that whenever Section 41-A Cr.P.C. notice is issued/whenever the bail is obtained by the accused, concerned police shall address a letter to the Commissioner and the Commissioner in turn shall address a letter to the Immigration Authorities to close the LOC.
5. In the instant case, the petitioner has obtained bail from the competent Court but still the respondents police are continuing the LOC against the petitioner without any basis.

6. Accordingly, the Writ Petition is allowed and the respondent No.4 i.e., Station House Officer,
Banjara Hills Police Station Hyderabad, is directed to address a letter to the Commissioner, who in turn shall address a letter to the Immigration Authorities, as expeditiously as possible, to close the LOC issued against the petitioner.
Pending miscellaneous applications, if any, shall stand closed.
There shall be no order as to costs.
SCS Vaddevalli Lalitha Saran Kumar vs Union Of India
